props.title: Raid on Entebbe

sections.content: Raid on Entebbe (1976) marks a pivotal moment in terrorism-themed cinema, arriving just months after the actual Israeli rescue operation in Uganda. Director Irvin Kershner (who later directed The Empire Strikes Back (1980)) crafted this taut thriller alongside competing production Victory at Entebbe (1976), though Kershner's version emerged as the definitive telling. The film established a template for military rescue operation movies, influencing works like Delta Force (1986) and Zero Dark Thirty (2012) with its meticulous attention to tactical details and escalating tension.

sections.content: The film's documentary-style approach, mixing archival footage with dramatization, influenced a whole subgenre of quick-turnaround docudramas about recent events. United 93 (2006) and Zero Dark Thirty (2012) would later perfect this hybrid format. Charles Bronson's restrained performance as Dan Shomron marked a departure from his typical vigilante roles, while Peter Finch delivered one of his final performances as Yitzhak Rabin before his Oscar-winning role in Network (1976).

The political complexities of the Entebbe crisis are handled with surprising nuance for a 1970s television film. Unlike later, more jingoistic military rescue films like Navy SEALs (1990), Raid on Entebbe attempts to contextualize the Palestinian hijackers' motivations while never justifying their actions. This balanced approach influenced later films like Munich (2005) and Paradise Now (2005). SUBHEAD: Impact on Military Operation Films

sections.content: The film's influence on tactical military operation cinema cannot be overstated. The meticulous recreation of the raid sequence, with its emphasis on preparation, timing, and precise execution, created a blueprint followed by films like Navy SEALs (1990), Black Hawk Down (2001), and Zero Dark Thirty (2012). The tension-building techniques - including the use of split-second timing and multiple perspective coverage - became standard features of the genre.
